killington.note: Good evening, Beast family, We’re kicking off April under some darker skies, but the surfaces are riding smooth and staying playful. Spring is making its move and there’s still plenty of fun to be had across the mountain. Clouds stick around Thursday with temps topping out near 33° at the base and 37° at the peak, with a breezy southeast wind keeping things feeling a bit sharper. There’s a chance of some freezing rain and snow showers rolling through at times. Our grooming team is charging full steam ahead on a normal plan, with crews resurfacing trails as coverage allows. You’ll find fresh passes on Reason, Full House, Upper Bittersweet, Outer Limits, The Northway, and more as they make their rounds. Be sure to check out the Lifts & Trails Report for the full list of groomers. Even though our groomers are being smart about what they resurface, we still have ample depth across the mountain and surfaces are skiing & riding nice and soft. Conditions may be variable in spots with areas ranging from wet granular to machine-groomed hard pack, although most of the turns are easily edge-able. Head over to Bear for more fun shreds on Skyeburst and Wildfire while that Black Diamond is still shredding. Please note that areas of thin cover are beginning to show as we move through this incoming weather pattern. Ski Patrol is actively monitoring conditions, marking hazards and noting where walking may be required. At this time, the Learn to Ski & Ride Area does have walking required, with the best beginner terrain available over on Snowshed Slope. As we continue into spring, our grooming team will keep pushing snow around and patching up those thinner spots where coverage allows. Looking ahead, we’re getting ready for one of our signature spring events, the Bear Mountain Mogul Challenge, returning this weekend. It’s always a great time at Bear with big bumps, big energy, and plenty of action. Registration is currently full for competitors but not for volunteers! Volunteers will be provided with lunch for the day & will earn a free Killington lift ticket voucher, good for a calendar year, for each completed shift. Roles are available working both indoors & outdoors, so please check the descriptions of each position to make sure you are comfortable in the given role. Please note that volunteer shifts for this event are limited so click here if you’re looking to help out! Even if you're not competing or volunteering, come be a part of the scene and catch all the action from the sidelines. We are scheduled to have 12 lifts spinning with key lifts open at 9:00 a.m. and the North Ridge Quad scheduled at 9:30 a.m. Please note: Although we will be running a bonus weekend over at Skyeship this weekend, Stage I will be closed until Friday. On the kparks front, our Bear parks, Dream Maker and The Stash, are firing with a full lineup of features. Over on Ramshead, Timberline continues to shine with 44 features, 5 jumps, and a halfpipe. Our Parks Crew recently refreshed features in Timberline and gave the halfpipe a fresh cut. Easy Street and Lil’ Stash are also dialed in for fun progression options. Check the Terrain Parks Report for all the details. Get out there and have fun! - Evan Operating Day: 141 Season passes for 26/27 are now on sale! Lock in the lowest price on Beast 365 or Winter Unlimited passes with lots of perks, plus free skiing & riding for the rest of this spring. And there's more good news for families: Youth & Child pass pricing has been significantly reduced for next season, with over $300 in savings on Beast 365 access. Lifts Key lifts operate seven days a week from 9:00 a.m. to 4:00 p.m. on Monday through Friday, and from 8:00 a.m. to 4:00 p.m. on Saturday and Sunday. The North Ridge Quad will open at 9:30 a.m. on weekdays and 8:00 a.m. on weekends, the Canyon Quad will spin from 10:00 a.m. to 3:30 p.m. Monday, Wednesday, Friday and 9:00 a.m. to 4:00 p.m. on weekends, and the Sunrise Village Triple will spin until 3:00 p.m. on weekdays and 4:00 p.m. on weekends. A note for our snowboarders: Thanks to our new cabins on the Skyeship Gondola, we're asking you to please utilize the snowboard racks outside of each cabin. If the racks are entirely full, please put your boards underneath the seats. This differs from our K-1 Gondola, where all snowboards should be brought inside the cabins. Just remember: outside Skyeship, inside K-1! The Tubing Park presented by bubly is closed for the season. copper mountain.note: Good morning everybody! Just like that, it's April 1st. A trace a new snow to mention this morning as of 430am, but hopefully things are just getting started. A few inches are possible by sundown tonight with more snow inbound for Thursday and Friday. Temps today will hover around 32F at mid-mountain and westerly winds will blow at 10-20mph with gusts possible into the 40s. Remember, as this new snow stacks up (hopefully), you're going to experience a wide variety of conditions out there left from several days of above average temps. Expect hazards that were visible yesterday to slowly disappear, but not completely go away. Stay on your toes! Hopefully Mother Nature isn't playing an April Fools joke on us, but just to be sure, make sure to do your best snow dance. Have a great day!

snowbird.note: Gooooood morning Snowbird! It’s Owen, with your snow report for Wednesday. Mountain Update: Regular 9 am to 4 pm hours return today, Wednesday, April 1. Guys. It did the thing. The tide is rising on Surf Season. 7” overnight. Another 2” - 5” projected throughout today. More snow coming Thursday and Friday. We’re back to 9 am - 4 pm hours (y’all can stop complaining about the hours now, I see your comments). Things are looking up - which is also where the best skiing will be today. The upper mountain, above around 9,000 feet will have the best turns, but as temperatures drop throughout this week, so will the snow levels and lower mountain skiing will improve. We'll have a high of 40° today but, with the heavier snow, you may want to bring some dry layers to change into. I will also say, be cautious today, especially off-piste as a lot of the stuff that’s melted off over the past week will now have a thin layer covering it. It may still be Surf Season, but don’t end it early with a shark attack. It’ll keep filling back in, so don’t worry, you can dial it back up tomorrow and Friday. Dare I say it - we are so back. Today is Play Forever Wednesday . $5 of your ticket will be donated to a non-profit of the week that is dedicated to bettering the environment, providing local relief or broadening participation in outdoor activities. This week, we are supporting First Step House, which provides a continuum of care with four supportive pillars, including behavioral health treatment, housing (case management and physical housing), on-site medical services and supportive employment. Click the link to learn more. If you haven't yet gotten your Chickadee Fever badge on the Snowbird App, now is the time! The Chickadee Lift will close for the 2025-26 season for replacement on April 6th. The new Chickadee Lift is expected to reopen for summer operations in July. ALL uphill travel is closed. Don’t be that guy (or gal). Please remember to ski and ride in control, if you don’t, you’re gonna have a bad time. It's high tide at Surf Season, so to quote that one guy, "drop in, just smack the lip, wapow." Go get pitted today. #GMTB
